kjv: an hundred thousand rams, with the wool
mine: the wool of a hundred thousand rams
note: Hebrew me'ah elef eilim tsamer, "a hundred thousand rams, wool", is most naturally read as the wool of the rams (the fleece was the tribute), not rams plus their wool.
Hebrew minchah here is the regular morning grain offering; "meat" in 1611 meant food in general, and today suggests flesh.
Hebrew qetsef gadol al-Yisra'el is wrath (normally divine) coming upon Israel; whose wrath is unstated, and the KJV's "indignation against" can suggest merely human outrage at Israel.
